# The guide block ledger.
#
# Every fenced block of every embedded guide is declared here, keyed by the
# guide's file and the one-based line its opening marker stands on. The rule
# this replaces forbade a block whose first line opened with a dollar sign and
# told authors to write the command without one, which is the spelling that
# made a block invisible to it. A ledger over blocks has no spelling an author
# can choose to evade: a block nobody declares fails, however it is written.
#
# `shows=` says what the block is and carries its own check:
#
#   commands  Every non-blank line is a command the reader types, beginning
#             with `dinah `. A line opening `$ ` and an output line are both
#             refused, because a block showing output is a transcript nothing
#             drives.
#   json      The block parses through encoding/json. A block showing two
#             members of an object rather than a whole document declares
#             `fragment=members` with a reason, and is parsed inside a
#             wrapping pair of braces. A block that parses on its own may not
#             declare it.
#   table     The block draws a table the tool renders, and `command=` names
#             the command. The block's header row is held against the drawn
#             one, and nothing else is, because the data rows are invented for
#             the lesson and the separator row's widths follow them.
#   shell     The block drives a shell rather than Dinah, so nothing here runs
#             it. It requires a reason.
#   tree      The block draws a directory tree. It requires a reason naming
#             what holds the tree, or why nothing can.
